title: Build accretive whole-system semantic optimizer
description: Deliver one executable closed-loop optimizer for any new or existing system. In greenfield mode it constructs competing semantic architectures and implementations from a purpose/environment envelope. In brownfield mode it recovers the living model and repeatedly removes accidental structure. Beads track implementation dependencies; working systems and measured improvements are the deliverable.
acceptance_criteria: The same engine and schemas construct a verified greenfield system and autonomously land at least two distinct verified improvements on a held-out Linux-testable brownfield target, rebuild the model after each, revisit every declared metric, and emit only envelope-and-grammar-relative stationarity after a confirming full sweep.

title: Implement living optimization state and computed frontier
description: Represent either an empty greenfield subject or a pinned existing implementation, together with the evidence-bound semantic model, purpose/environment envelope, declared metric vector, transformation coverage, candidate frontier, counterexamples, and open unknowns as one content-addressed campaign state. Replace caller-asserted exhaustion with computed coverage.
acceptance_criteria: One state schema initializes both greenfield and brownfield campaigns; the controller rejects a fixture that merely asserts generators exhausted, distinguishes open, budget-exhausted, frontier-set, envelope-stationary, and bounded-exhaustive states, and requires a second unchanged complete sweep before stationarity.
close_reason: Implemented kerf.optimization-campaign.v1 and kerf-cycle: shared greenfield/brownfield state, content-addressed search/decision identities, computed versioned generator coverage and budget exhaustion, exact Kerf Pareto frontier, open/frontier-set/envelope-stationary/bounded-exhaustive/budget-with-unknowns statuses, and two-sweep stationarity. Verified by 9 focused cycle/CLI tests, full semantic-architecture tests, strict clippy, model/Kerf/seam checks, and UBS exit 0.

title: Generate proof-carrying transformations without a named seam
description: Build a deterministic transformation registry and whole-system matcher for both imagined and existing subjects. Initial families are capability construction, behavioral quotient/factor realization, authority consolidation, isomorphic simplification, and split/fuse/relocate including new-module birth and death. Every candidate binds to a parent state and carries a predicted metric delta, proof obligations, falsifier, and nonclaims.
acceptance_criteria: Given only a purpose envelope for greenfield, or a repository root plus envelope for brownfield, the engine produces nontrivial implementation or refactoring candidates from at least three families without a hand-authored seam; file-size-only proposals and candidates without verification obligations are rejected.
close_reason: Implemented kerf.transformation-request/batch.v1 and kerf-generate with content-bound registry, envelope hashing, deterministic greenfield and brownfield whole-system generation, five transformation families, semantic witness admission, all-metric qualitative predictions, proof obligations, falsifiers, nonclaims, source traversal bounds, replay validation, and file-size-witness rejection. Verified by 9 generator/CLI tests, full semantic-architecture test suite, strict clippy, JSM validation, and UBS exit 0.

title: Apply verify measure and rebuild after every accepted change
description: Implement the closed execution loop: isolate a candidate, materialize the patch, run protected behavior and negative controls, measure declared coordinates, independently rebuild the semantic model, compare predicted and observed semantic deltas, accept or reject, retain counterexamples, and refresh the frontier.
acceptance_criteria: A candidate cannot be accepted without a real patch, identity-bound pre/post evidence, a measured improvement on at least one declared coordinate, no forbidden regression, a closed predicted-versus-measured ledger, and a rebuilt model naming the new revision.

title: Pass the two-move real-code metabolism experiment
description: Run the engine on a held-out Linux-testable target with no named seam. It must land one verified nontrivial improvement, rebuild autonomously, then discover and land a distinct second improvement. Compare against ordinary expert inspection and the existing isomorphic-refactor baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Two distinct code improvements are accepted sequentially without human model re-authoring or seam selection; cumulative measurements improve the declared frontier with zero protected regressions; suggestions, receipts, renames, or file moves alone do not pass.

title: Escape local minima and validate ecological adaptation
description: After the metabolism works, add cleanup-ranked multi-step migrations, neutral representation walks, multiscale large-neighborhood search, greenfield re-derivation, and held-out environment or requirement perturbations. Retain only mechanisms that beat the simpler search.
acceptance_criteria: The engine escapes a constructed single-move fixed point to a verified better endpoint, and its adaptability prediction ranks held-out real change burden better than static structural metrics; failed mechanisms are removed rather than documented as capability.

title: Accrete validated mechanisms into the canonical skills
description: Update Semantic Architecture, Seam Topology, Behavioral Factorization, and executor routing only after project evidence demonstrates reusable value. Keep the user-facing workflow unified and skill manuals concise; place deterministic behavior in scripts and schemas.
acceptance_criteria: Each skill change names the observed pilot evidence, reusable mechanism, consumer, and falsifier; validation and forward tests pass; no skill claims an optimization capability that did not produce verified code improvement.

title: Demonstrate cross-project transfer and improve the improvement loop
description: Run the validated engine on a second unrelated repository, compare transferred generator priors against cold start, and improve how future project evidence proposes, validates, admits, demotes, or retires transformation families.
acceptance_criteria: Transferred priors improve discovery or verification efficiency on a held-out repository without reducing accepted quality; otherwise the transfer claim is falsified and removed. The admission loop uses measured deltas and prediction error rather than finding counts or model agreement.

title: Self-host greenfield construction and brownfield improvement
description: Use the current skill system to construct the semantic optimizer from its purpose envelope and compile that model into its acceptance harness and implementation work. Once the engine can execute, point it back at this repository and require a real verified improvement. Both routes must use the same state, generator, evidence, and stopping machinery.
acceptance_criteria: The greenfield model directly drives at least one implemented controller capability and its executable acceptance test; later self-application lands at least one nontrivial verified improvement in this repository, rebuilds its own model, and exposes another frontier or honest bounded stationarity. A design document or skill prose edit alone does not pass.
